articles.title: Complaint alleges irregularities in GFI camp funds, treasurer rejects charges
articles.summary: KOLKATA: A complaint submitted to the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Sunday has accused the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI) of possible diversion
articles.body: KOLKATA: A complaint submitted to the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Sunday has accused the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI) of possible diversion and misappropriation of govt funds released for national coaching camps in Bhubaneswar, alleging that athletes, coaches and vendors are yet to receive payments despite the federation submitting a utilisation certificate (UC) for the expenditure.In a representation to SAI, a copy of which is with TOI, former international gymnast and GFI general body member Rakesh Kumar Patra alleged that a little more than Rs 14.42 lakh sanctioned for men’s and women’s artistic gymnastics camps held ahead of the Asian Championships was shown as utilised, even though several liabilities remain unsettled.The complaint by the national coach claims that hospitality provider Swastik Hospitality is owed nearly Rs 12 lakh, while physiotherapist Yash Jaiswal and several gymnasts and coaches, including Dipa Karmakar, are awaiting reimbursements.Seeking an independent financial and vigilance inquiry, Patra has also sought scrutiny of GFI president Sudhir Mital, treasurer Kaushik Bidiwala and the chartered accountant firm Narender Singh & Co., which certified the utilisation certificate.Responding to the allegations, Bidiwala denied any irregularity in the issuance of the utilisation certificate. “A utilisation certificate cannot be issued without proper documentation and supporting records. If the documents are not available, even the chartered accountant will not certify it,” Bidwala told TOI.He said allegations and certification of expenditure were separate matters and maintained that the UC process involved verification of original documents and proofs.On the issue of pending reimbursements, Bidiwala said delays, if any, could be linked to procedural requirements rather than withholding of payments. “If any reimbursements are pending, it is not because there is an intention to withhold anyone’s money. There may be processing delays, but the money will not be stopped and beneficiaries will receive their payments,” he said.The treasurer added that he was focused on the welfare of the sport and cautioned that prolonged disputes could hurt gymnastics’ image and discourage parents from encouraging children to take up the discipline.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “He worked 100 hours a week so I could chase my dream” - How Rory McIlroy and his father turned sacrifice, Masters glory and illness into an unbreakable bond
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy’s eighth Race to Dubai title in November 2026 was about much more than another golfing record.
articles.body: Rory McIlroy’s eighth Race to Dubai title in November 2026 was about much more than another golfing record. The Northern Irishman fought back tears as he dedicated the achievement to his father, Gerry McIlroy, who is recovering from a life-saving double-lung transplant. After an 18-month health battle, Gerry underwent surgery in Cleveland in September. Rory had spent nine days beside him in intensive care in October before visiting him again ahead of his trip to the Middle East. His father’s request was simple: “Rors, go and win me the Race to Dubai”. Rory went on to secure his fifth consecutive and eighth overall title, matching Colin Montgomerie’s record.How did Gerry McIlroy sacrifice so much for Rory’s golf dream?Rory’s journey began in Holywood, Northern Ireland, where his love for golf started when he was still a toddler. His father, Gerry, was a keen golfer himself and quickly noticed how much his young son enjoyed the sport. Rory was soon asking to visit Holywood Golf Club regularly, and his parents did everything they could to give him the chance to improve.Money was not easy to come by in the McIlroy household. Gerry took on several jobs, working as a barman and cleaner, while his wife, Rosie, worked night shifts at a 3M factory. Gerry’s working week reportedly reached 100 hours as the couple tried to pay for their son’s golf lessons, equipment and trips to tournaments.Their sacrifices meant that family time and holidays often had to wait. Gerry would work long hours, while Rosie took factory shifts, but neither wanted their financial situation to stop Rory from following his ambition.The Washington Post reported on how Rory practised at home as a young child. He would chip golf balls down the hallway and into the family’s washing machine. It was an unusual practice area, but it showed how early his interest in the sport had begun.His parents also made sure that his talent was guided by the right people. Gerry helped introduce him to golf coach Michael Bannon, who played an important role in his early development.Rory has spoken about what his parents did to help him. Reflecting on their sacrifices, he once said: “I’ll never be able to repay Mum and Dad for what they did”.How did Gerry McIlroy’s 500-1 bet come true?Gerry’s faith in his son was not limited to taking him to practice sessions and helping him pay for golf. He also backed Rory’s future with a remarkable bet.In 2004, when Rory was just 15, Gerry and three friends placed a £400 bet at odds of 500-1 on the youngster winning The Open Championship before turning 26.At the time, Rory was still an amateur, and winning one of golf’s biggest tournaments was a huge ambition. But his father believed he had the ability to reach that level.Ten years later, the bet became reality. Rory won The Open at Royal Liverpool in 2014, aged 25, beating Sergio Garcia and Rickie Fowler by two shots. He lifted the Claret Jug, claimed his third major championship and made his father’s early confidence look extraordinary.The story became even more special because Gerry had backed his son long before he became one of the biggest names in golf. It was not simply a bet on a future champion. It was a reflection of the belief he had in Rory from the beginning.How did Rory McIlroy make Masters history in 2025 and 2026?While Gerry’s support helped Rory reach the professional game, his son went on to build a career that few golfers can match.Rory won four major championships by the age of 25, including the 2014 Open. However, the Masters remained the one major trophy missing from his collection.His wait finally ended in April 2025. Rory defeated Justin Rose in a playoff at Augusta National to win his first Green Jacket and complete the career Grand Slam. He became only the sixth golfer to win all four men’s major championships.The victory carried years of pressure and disappointment. Rory had come close to winning the Masters before, most painfully in 2011, when he lost a four-shot final-round lead.Then came another historic moment in April 2026. Rory successfully defended his Masters title, joining Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods as the only players to win back-to-back Green Jackets.For Gerry and Rosie, who had spent years supporting their son’s dream, watching him achieve that feat was another special moment in a journey that had started in their modest home in Northern Ireland.What happened to Gerry McIlroy, and how did Rory honour him in Dubai?The McIlroy family faced a difficult period in 2026 when Gerry’s health deteriorated. According to Rory’s comments after the Race to Dubai victory, his father had been dealing with the condition for around 18 months. His treatment eventually reached a point where a double-lung transplant became necessary.Gerry underwent the operation in September 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. The 67-year-old remained in hospital for two months as he recovered. Rory spent nine days with him in intensive care and was unsure whether he would be able to travel for his upcoming tournaments.The golfer later explained that his father’s medical team had helped the family through the difficult period. He was reassured by the doctors and nurses looking after Gerry and felt comfortable returning to competition.Before travelling to Abu Dhabi, Rory visited his father again. Gerry had one request for his son: “Rors, go and win me the Race to Dubai”.Those words stayed with Rory during the final stretch of the season.At the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai on November 15, Rory produced a final-round 67. Although Tyrrell Hatton won the tournament, Rory finished second and collected enough points to secure the season-long Race to Dubai crown.It was his fifth consecutive title and eighth overall, bringing him level with Colin Montgomerie’s record.Speaking about his father after the achievement, Rory became emotional and said: “This one’s for him”.He also explained how much Gerry had influenced his life, calling him his biggest supporter and the person who introduced him to golf.For Rory, the achievement had a personal meaning that went beyond another record. His father had spent years helping him reach the biggest stages in golf. This time, with Gerry watching from his hospital bed in Cleveland, Rory had something special to give back.The boy who once practised with a plastic club in his family home had grown into a champion with six major titles, a career Grand Slam and eight Race to Dubai crowns. But the words that mattered most before his latest victory came from the same man who had helped him take his first steps in golf.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: LSU guard MiLaysia Fulwiley absent for the No. 9 Tigers' game against Troy after recent arrest
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La (AP) — LSU senior guard MiLaysia Fulwiley, who was arrested after allegedly attempting to flee a traffic stop Saturday night, was not in the...
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La (AP) — LSU senior guard MiLaysia Fulwiley, who was arrested after allegedly attempting to flee a traffic stop Saturday night, was not in the lineup or on the team's bench for the No. 9 Tigers' home game against Troy on Monday night.

Florida transfer Laila Reynolds, who came off the bench for the first four games of this season, started in Fulwiley's place.

LSU coach Kim Mulkey did not address Fulwiley's status on Sunday or before the game on Monday, and it remained unclear to those outside the locker room whether she would be with the team until the Tigers came out for pre-game warm-ups.

The university stated on Sunday that it was aware of the arrest but would not comment further on a pending legal matter.

East Baton Rouge District Attorney Hillar Moore said Monday he was still awaiting reports on the matter from the law enforcement departments involved.

The traffic stop occurred around the time the Texas vs. LSU football game was ending on Saturday night.

The Louisiana State Police, who assist with traffic flow around 102,000-seat Tiger Stadium on football game days, have said they intend to collect and make available all available video footage from body and dashboard cameras. Police also indicated they would seek security camera footage from buildings in the area where the stop occurred and where Fulwiley was ultimately taken into custody.

Authorities allege that an officer tried to stop the 21-year-old Fulwiley after observing her weaving through traffic, and that she drove away from the scene, the right front side of her vehicle striking a police vehicle.

She allegedly sought to cut through a store parking lot before her vehicle was blocked by responding police.

Fulwiley was booked into East Baton Rouge Parish Prison on charges including aggravated battery, flight from an officer, aggravated assault and resisting an officer.

Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points per game this season and scored a season-high 23 points during LSU's 101-37 victory over Denver on Friday.

articles.title: ‘He Has To Look Joe Buck In His Face’ — ESPN Legend Applauds Troy Aikman’s ‘Professionalism’ in MNF Booth Despite Contract Stalemate
articles.summary: Troy Aikman’s Monday nights have come with a lot more than football games this fall. The partnership between Aikman and Joe Buck has run for about 25 years,...
articles.body:
Troy Aikman's Monday nights have come with a lot more than football games this fall.

The partnership between Aikman and Joe Buck has run for about 25 years, first at FOX and then at ESPN. Buck signed a six-year extension worth about $108 million. But Aikman is playing out the final year of his deal and does not have a new one in hand.

In a Monday interview with Yahoo Sports, former SportsCenter anchor Linda Cohn weighed in on how Aikman finds himself between a rock and a hard place while his contract remains unresolved.

Linda Cohn Addresses Chemistry Between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck

Her clip surfaced the same day ESPN's Monday Night Football has the Los Angeles Chargers visiting the Baltimore Ravens. Cohn turned to the partnership itself. "He has to look Joe Buck in his face. I don't know how the relationship is now. It looks cold as ice right now, of course, in the last month."

Notably, the tension between the two became public in October, when Buck and Aikman argued about their standing with ESPN before the Oct. 12 Los Angeles Rams-Buffalo Bills game at SoFi Stadium.

From there, Cohn walked through everything the job still asks of Aikman besides Buck, on the air and away from it. "But to be able to stand there and be professional and analyze a football game and not only do the game for three and a half hours, but to do everything that comes with that game, travel, meetings with coaches and players, it's just absolutely absurd."

Aikman, for his part, has already laid out his plan. "There's probably a time and a place for all that. I don't know if now is the time. … I'll broadcast through this season, and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens.

"But I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot might be," he said on Oct. 15.

In mid-October, Cohn had already taken aim at ESPN, saying its treatment of Aikman's contract situation was "not professional."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

The Athletic's Andrew Marchand had also reported there had been "an off-air unease between the duo through the first five weeks of this season, intensified by the fact ESPN chose Buck over Aikman for a new contract." He confirmed that talks with Aikman are on hold, and that in executives' eyes, the strain between the two partners may weigh most of all.

"It is clear ESPN has taken Buck's side in the pending divorce," Marchand wrote. He also outlined why Buck sees it differently.

Aikman took Buck's quiet extension as a betrayal, but Buck saw it as no different from how Aikman had handled his own previous negotiations. When Aikman negotiated that earlier deal, Marchand wrote, he "did so without knowing if Buck, who had a year left on his Fox deal, would be able to follow."

So the routine Cohn described is set to go on for months. The two are slated to stay paired through the rest of the season and the Feb. 14 broadcast of Super Bowl LXI.

articles.title: Highlights, MVP, and Twitter reactions to Kentucky Wildcats beating Grambling State
articles.body:
After a first half with carryover vibes from Friday night, Kentucky Basketball flipped the switch in the second half on both ends of the floor. Those second 20 minutes are what this Cats team should look like, with Kentucky pulling away from Grambling State for an 88-57 win.

Kentucky outscored the Tigers 52-29 in the second half, turning a six-point halftime lead into a 29-point win. After getting pounded on the glass by Northern Arizona, the Cats won the rebounding battle 49-33 and 15-10 on the offensive glass Monday night. Kentucky also had 22 assists on 31 made shots, while holding the Tigers to just 29.8 percent shooting and 5-24 from three-point range.

With Diallo running the offense and Moreno finishing possessions, the Cats may have found a combination in their backcourt and frontcourt. Diallo finished with 12 points and nine rebounds and assists, while also adding two steals in 32 minutes. Moreno exploded for 22 points and 12 rebounds, adding four steals. He also added three blocks. Six of his rebounds were offensive, and six were defensive.

Kentucky got off to a good start offensively, racing out to a 19-8 lead less than eight minutes into the game. But then, their offense went ice cold. Completely cold, they went over five minutes without scoring and missed 15 of 16 shots on top of that. Alex Wilkins, fittingly, stopped the freeze with two free throws. Braydon Hawthorne swished a three-pointer with just over four minutes remaining for the Cats' first field goal in eight minutes. That started a 7-0 run where the Cats made three straight shots to stretch a 22-21 lead to 29-21.

Grambling State cut the deficit to 33-30 late in the first half, but Mason Williams pulled up for a long three-pointer just as the time expired to give Kentucky a 36-30 lead at halftime.

The Wildcats shot just 34.3 percent from the field in the first half, but they were 5-13 fom three-point range. Kentucky also out-rebounded Grambling State 26-19 and 8-3 on the offensive glass. They had five steals, and Malachi Moreno and Zoom Diallo led the Cats with eight points in the first 20 minutes. Ironically, it was Diallo who led the Cats with seven rebounds and five assists.

Grambling State shot just 34.5 percent from the floor in the first half and 4-14 from three-point range. The Tigers had seven turnovers in the first half, allowing Kentucky to stay ahead or tied the entire 20 minutes.

Kentucky built on Williams' buzzer-beater to build a 17-point lead less than five minutes into the second half. The Cats started 6-10 from the field and 3-3 from three-point range. This is what it's supposed to look like. There was intensity. There was purpose. There was energy. In addition, shots were falling.

The lead gradually grew throughout the second half, with the Cats moving the ball and taking care of it. On the other side, there was defensive intensity in forcing the Tigers into a bad second-half shooting, making just 25 percent of their shots and 1-10 from three-point range. Grambling State also had seven turnovers to five assists in the second 20 minutes.

Ten different Cats scored at least two points Monday night, with four going for double figures. On a night where Alex Wilkins was held in check scoring and didn't even make a three-pointer, the Cats still won by 29 points.

Kentucky shot 59.4 percent from the field and 5-12 from three-point range in the second half, while out-rebounding the Tigers 23-14. The Cats also had 14 assists to just five turnovers and had five steals.

Kentucky vs. Grambling State Twitter Reactions

It was a swing of emotions for Big Blue Nation Monday night. Here are the best reactions from Big Blue Nation Twitter.

articles.title: Player Grades: Cavs vs Bulls – Donovan Mitchell scores 39 points
articles.summary: Mitchell looked like an All-NBA player tonight.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers took care of business against the Chicago Bulls in a 126-115 victory.

Grades are based on our usual expectations for each player.

39 points, 4 rebounds, 4 assists, 3 steals

Mitchell proved to everyone that he's still spry, rising up for a crushing alley-oop dunk off of Proctor's pass.

The Cavs have been workshopping the correct approach for Mitchell this season. That's led to some games where he isn't as aggressive as we've come to expect. Tonight, Mitchell picked his spots and asserted himself consistently.

The second half was when Mitchell really had it rolling. He was getting downhill with ease and broke Chicago's defense with his attacks. Mitchell poured in 18 points on a perfect 8-of-8 shooting in the fourth quarter. A tough pull-up three-pointer was the cherry on top, and a final dash to the hoop was the cherry on top of a fantastic scoring night.

Cleveland might be testing their luck with all of this positive quarterback play recently, but Harden was launching Hail Marys all night to Peyton Watson, as it seems there was a clear effort to beat the Bulls in transition. Harden threw at least four full-court passes to Watson, who was leaking out after contesting three-point attempts.

Having Harden be the outlet passer is one way to play with pace without asking a 37-year-old to run a marathon each night.

That said, Harden shot 3-for-10 from the floor.

Allen had a strong game on the glass, racking up 3 offensive rebounds in the first quarter and finishing the game with 6 second-chance opportunities. It feels like the Cavs are at their best when Allen is crushing it on the boards, and tonight was no different.

The Cavs haven't unlocked anything new from Watson offensively yet, as they are still waiting for him to rediscover his three-point jumper. Another poor shooting night has put a limit on how impactful Watson can be — but he's overall been a positive, especially on defense.

Watson left the game midway through the fourth quarter after taking a nasty fall onto his back.

17 points, 3 rebounds, 2 assists, 2 steals, 1 block

Proctor remained in the starting lineup tonight after his triple-double performance this weekend. He looked comfortable on the floor again, playing off-ball next to Mitchell and Harden while making a positive impact on both ends of the court.

10 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals

Thomas struggled with his outside shot tonight, shooting 1-for-7 from deep. Even so, being a threat to launch it from downtown is worth something. And Thomas managed to lean on his dribble to create good looks inside the paint and opportunities for his teammates.

Hezonja has been a bone-crushing presence for the Cavs. He's a monster on the glass and doesn't concede any ground defensively. Opponents can't move him on either end of the floor, and that makes him a valuable weapon to have.

Bryant has filled in nicely for both Mobley and Allen during this stretch where the bigs have been injured on and off. He gave more quality minutes tonight, providing a spark of energy and veteran leadership to the bench.

4 points, 6 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 block, 1 steal

Omier is earning every minute. He changed the dynamic of this game with his hustle in the second quarter, being always eager to attack the offensive glass or bury a defender with a deep seal in the post.

articles.title: Ben Johnson Emerges As a Contender For Coach Of The Year
articles.summary: Ben Johnson leads the 7-2 Bears to a division lead. See why experts rank him third for Coach of the Year and how the Simmons trade helped.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson has the Chicago Bears sitting at 7-2 and tied for the lead in the NFC North midway through the 2026 season. ESPN analyst Bill Barnwell placed Johnson at No. 3 on his midseason list for Coach of the Year, ranking him just behind Kyle Shanahan and Liam Coen. The Bears are riding a four-game winning streak and have secured a spot as one of the top teams in the conference.

Johnson has guided the team to this position despite missing starting quarterback Caleb Williams for three games. Even after the All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons trade significantly improved the defense, the offense still ranks as a top-five unit in the league. This combination of a high-scoring offense and a strengthened defense makes Johnson a clear favorite for the award.

Bill Barnwell, writing for ESPN, named his top three picks for the award at the midpoint of the season. Johnson sits at No. 3 on that list. He trails only San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan, who holds the top spot, and Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen, who is ranked second.

Local experts also see the Bears as a dominant force. A pre-Week 10 poll of NFC North beat writers for ESPN showed that three of the four writers placed the Bears at the top of their division rankings. Courtney Cronin noted the favorable schedule coming out of the bye week, pointing to matchups against the Saints and Dolphins. She highlighted that Johnson holds a perfect 7-0 record in November since arriving in Chicago.

Cronin added that the Bears have the most complete team in the division. She stated the offense scores 30.7 points per game when Williams is under center. The team has a top-tier offense and a defense that added a star player.

The acquisition of Jeffery Simmons has been a key factor in the Bears' success this season. Sando pointed out that Simmons has made an immediate impact on the defensive line. The new arrival has played 121 snaps in his first two games with the team.

Those two games have produced solid numbers for the defensive tackle. "Simmons had 10 tackles, including two sacks and an additional tackle for loss, while playing 121 snaps in his first two games with the Bears," Sando wrote on November 16th, 2026, according to Heavy.com . His presence allows the rest of the defense to play more aggressively.

One specific play highlighted his style of play during the recent win over Tampa Bay. "His downfield tackle in a 27-24 victory over Tampa Bay showcased an all-out playing style few men his size can match," Sando wrote. It demonstrates a high level of intensity that can change the momentum of a game.

Sando believes this specific type of effort is crucial for winning. "It's the type of move that elevates contenders," he wrote. The Bears now have a player who brings that energy to the defensive front. This elevates the entire team's status from a good squad to a potential championship threat.

Ben Johnson has spoken directly about how Simmons fits into the team's overall philosophy. He believes the impact of the new player has been significant. "I think it's been fairly dramatic, there's no doubt about it," Johnson said via NBC Sports. The coach sees the change in the team's approach as a major positive development.

Johnson focuses on consistency in how the team operates every day. He told his players to maintain the same routine in the building and on game day. "We keep preaching to our guys the consistency of how we go about our business, what we do in the building, and what we do on game day," Johnson said. This focus on routine helps the team perform at a high level even when facing tough opponents.

The coach believes that good teams do not change their approach based on the opponent. "That's what good teams do," Johnson said. He also emphasized the need for energy throughout the week. "Really, that's what great teams do, is bring that same juice an energy throughout the week and into the game as well." The Bears have won their last four games.

Johnson's leadership has helped the team handle the pressure of a tight division race. The Bears now share the same record of 7-2 with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions. The coaching staff has kept the team focused on winning rather than worrying about the standings.

The race for the NFC North title remains very tight. Minnesota and Detroit both share the same 7-2 record as Chicago. The Vikings beat the Bears earlier this season, and they also defeated Green Bay recently. The Lions have a strong offense that could be a game-changer in the title race. Only Lions writer Eric Woodyard dismissed the Bears hype because Detroit beat Chicago twice last season.

Kevin Seifert, a Vikings insider, added a note of caution regarding the division standings. "But the one thing to watch is that both of their losses this season were in the division," Seifert said. "That could be detrimental in a division tiebreaker if that is how the season ends." This means the Bears must win their remaining division games to secure the title.

Rob Demovsky of the Packers beat gave the Bears their props despite their 0-2 start in division play. "The Bears are the best team in the division despite being 0-2," Demovsky said. The team faced a formidable Vikings defense in Week 2 and was without their quarterback during the Week 5 game in Green Bay, he noted. The remaining schedule includes three division games at Soldier Field and one on the road.

The final stretch includes the Packers at home, the Lions at home, and the Vikings on the road. The Bears have the division's most well-rounded team. Despite a difficult road ahead involving four division games against competitive NFC North opponents, the Bears have clearly shown that they compete with any team in the NFL.

The Bears have eight remaining regular-season games to build on their current success.

articles.title: Virginia Tech basketball: Hokies defeat Richmond 85-68
articles.body:
The Virginia Tech Hokies defeated the Richmond Spiders 85-68 on Monday night at Cassell Coliseum to improve to 5-0 on the season.

The Hokies dominated the first half, opening up a 20-point lead before Richmond scored the final basket before halftime. Senior guard Jaylen Curry led the Hokies in the first half with 10 points, while senior guard Butta Johnson came off the bench and scored nine, all from 3-point range.

Tech dominated the boards early, holding a 23-12 advantage in the first half. Remarkably, the Hokies built up a big lead with little help from junior guard Ben Hammond, who went scoreless in the first 20 minutes. He missed all seven of his shot attempts, but did dish out four assists.

The Spiders started the second half red hot, scoring the first 15 points, going on a 17-0 run to cut Virginia Tech's lead to 41-38. Senior forward Miles Heide's tip-in three minutes into the second half appeared to wake up the Hokies.

VT would then go on a 12-2 run to open its lead back up to 14. Richmond's threat ended there. Hammond finally caught fire early in the second half, scoring 13 points in the first 12 minutes on 5-for-7 shooting. He finished with a team-high 15 points and seven assists. Junior forward Amani Hansberry also scored 15, while junior guard Tyler Johnson finished with a double-double off the bench, scoring 10 points and pulling down a game-high 11 rebounds. The 6-foot-5 Johnson entered the game as VT's leading rebounder at over seven per game.

Virginia Tech shot 50% from the field, made 10 of 23 from beyond the arc (43%), and went 17-for-21 from the free-throw line. The Hokies outrebounded the Spiders 33-28 and forced 15 Richmond turnovers.

The Hokies responded well after the Spiders opened the second half on a massive run. Once Tech weathered that storm, the game was essentially over.

Next up for Virginia Tech is the Shriner's Children's Charleson Classic in Charleston, South Carolina, on Friday and Sunday. The Hokies will play Northwestern (Big Ten) on Friday (3 p.m. ET) and Oklahoma State (Big 12) on Sunday (3 p.m. ET).

articles.title: Calvary cross country coach Richard Laninga named state Coach of the Year after title
articles.summary: Back-to-back state championships have led Calvary cross country coach Richard Laninga to a statewide award.
articles.body:
Calvary Schools of Holland doesn't have a lot of sports to choose from.

One of the smallest high schools in the state, it has been a basketball school with volleyball and soccer at times.

But the past few years, the Owls have become a state power in cross country, winning back-to-back MHSAA Division 4 state championships at Michigan International Speedway.

Coach Richard Laninga has been at the helm of this rise the past few seasons and molded the Owls into state champions.

After the second title, Laninga was selected by the MITCA Board as the 2026 Boys Michigan Cross Country Coach of the Year for the U.S. Track & Field and Cross Country Coaches Association.

It is the first time a Calvary coach has earned the state's coach of the year award in any sport.

"Coach Laninga absolutely deserves winning Coach of the Year. He comes to practice every day with a smile on his face and connects relationally with every member of the team," Calvary runner Noah Schipper said. "Mr. Laninga cares more about growing each runner's character than winning, but he also works hard to put together an awesome training plan for the team. I don't know where I would be in my running career without him."

And the program isn't going anywhere, either.

Most of the Calvary runners are underclassmen and will be back looking for an unprecedented three-peat.

Contact sports editor Dan D'Addona at Dan.D'Addona@hollandsentinel.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter @DanDAddona or Facebook @HollandSentinelSport s.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals S Andrew Wingard to miss a while with hand/wrist injury
articles.summary: Despite playing every snap on Sunday, safety Andrew Wingard will be out a while with an injury.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals safety Andrew Wingard missed three games earlier this season with a knee injury. He is going to miss some time again with another injury.

Head coach Mike LaFleur announced to reporters on Monday that Wingard suffered a hand or wrist injury on Sunday in the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and will "be out for an extended period of time."

Wingard played all 76 snaps in the game on defense on Sunday and led the team with 11 tackles. He also broke up a pass.

On the season, he has played in seven games and has 53 total tackles, three tackles for loss, an interception, two pass breakups and a forced fumble.

LaFleur didn't say whether Wingard would go on injured reserve, but in his absence, it means either Dadrion Taylor-Demerson or Kitan Crawford will move into the starting lineup.

The Cardinals have three games until the bye week.

articles.title: Chargers’ Justin Herbert calls his own number on tough opening touchdown run vs. Ravens
articles.summary: Coach Jim Harbaugh’s Los Angeles Chargers hit the road to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Baltimore, providing a stage for Justin Herbert to shine on after a...
articles.body:
Coach Jim Harbaugh 's Los Angeles Chargers hit the road to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Baltimore, providing a stage for Justin Herbert to shine on after a wild pre-game warmup . Injury updates to David Njoku and Denzel Perryman made the Chargers' task appear taller, but Herbert took matters into his own hands with a huge run early in the game.

Herbert took off running on third-and-six from just outside the 22-yard-line of the Ravens, winding up with one of the best plays of the season on offense for Mike McDaniels' oft-maligned unit.

The Chargers led, 7-0, as Tre Harris caught a pass for 22 yards and they drove into Baltimore territory again with just over seven minutes left in the first quarter. The drive ended without anymore points for Los Angeles as the Ravens took over with a first and ten on their own ten-yard-line.

New Ravens starting QB Jacoby Brissett got off to a fairly slow start with 2-of-4 passing and nine yards for coach Jesse Minter's team. The Ravens had lost four games in a row, most recently by a score of 33-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars, heading into the game, and remained in playoff contention.

The Chargers looked dead in the water following their 0-8 start, but played with the pride of a team that wanted to secure its first win of the season. An injury to wide receiver Ladd McConkey kept him out of the game, but McDaniel pushed the right buttons early on as the Chargers kept applying the pressure to defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver's group.

Los Angeles is a far better team on paper than their record indicated, giving the Ravens plenty to think about as the game headed toward the second quarter.

articles.title: 💥Terrible transfer news for Chivas
articles.summary: As Chivas de Guadalajara enters the final stretch of the Apertura 2026 under Gabriel Milito, journalist Alex Ramírez revealed some discouraging news for fans...
articles.body:
As Chivas de Guadalajara enters the final stretch of the Apertura 2026 under Gabriel Milito, journalist Alex Ramírez revealed some discouraging news for fans: the club's management has no plans to make any big-name signings in the upcoming winter transfer window.

Banking on continuity and academy talent

Although fans were calling for marquee signings such as Erik Lira, Denzell García or Alí Ávila, Ramírez explained that Javier Mier and Alejandro Manzo will maintain a tight budget. The club will prioritize young talent coming through the academy and keeping forwards such as Ricardo Marín and Chuy Hernández, ruling out the arrival of a high-profile striker or defender.

This approach raises concerns ahead of competing on two fronts in 2027, particularly in defense, given Miguel Tapias's imminent departure, the uncertainty surrounding Ángel Chávez and Necaxa's permanent signing of Francisco Méndez.

articles.title: Fans, media react to Iowa basketball loss vs. Creighton
articles.summary: Here's how Iowa media and fans reacted to the Hawkeyes' Sunday loss against Creighton.
articles.body:
Despite a career-high 22-point performance from center Trevin Jirak and a valiant comeback attempt, Iowa basketball (2-2) fell to Creighton (3-1) on Sunday afternoon at the Casey's Center in Des Moines, 70-69.

Jirak's 22 points came from 5 for 10 shooting and 10 for 10 marksmanship at the free-throw line. The 6-foot-11, 249-pound center is the first Hawkeye since 2024 to make 10 or more free throws without a miss. Jirak also added six rebounds, four assists, and three steals.

Unfortunately, the only other Hawkeye to finish in double-figure scoring was Cooper Koch, who registered a double-double with 16 points and 10 rebounds. Iowa fell behind by as many as 14 points, turned the basketball over 15 times throughout the contest, and shot just 38% as a team.

The Hawkeyes had an opportunity to walk off the Bluejays, but Peyton McCollum's potential buzzer-beating 3-pointer didn't drop.
